title: Recognizing Invalid Setups
hook: Not every setup becomes a trade. Some fail after BOS #3, and some never finish.

launchpad.outcome: Recognize an invalidated zone (a 5M close beyond its far edge) and an incomplete sequence (no BOS #2 or no BOS #3), and make the no-trade decision.
launchpad.missionQuestion: When does a zone stop being an entry opportunity?

takeaways: After BOS #3, a 5M candle closing beyond the zone’s far edge makes the setup invalid.
For demand, the far edge is the zone’s low. For supply, it’s the zone’s high.
If price returns to an invalidated zone, it’s still not an entry.
If BOS #2 or BOS #3 never happens, the sequence is incomplete. No trade.

slides.headline: Some setups never become trades.
slides.line: A setup can fail after BOS #3, or never finish at all. Knowing when to walk away is part of the strategy.

slides.kicker: Step 1 · Three ways a setup fails
slides.headline: Invalid or incomplete means no trade.
slides.line: Tap each card. Each one stops the setup for a different reason.

cards.label: Invalidated
cards.sub: After BOS #3, a 5M candle closes beyond the zone’s far edge.

cards.label: No BOS #2
cards.sub: BOS #1 and Correction #1 happen, but the 5M never continues.

cards.label: No BOS #3
cards.sub: Correction #2 forms a potential zone, but BOS #3 never comes.

slides.headline: A close below the demand zone ends it.
slides.line: BOS #3 has activated this demand zone. Press the button and watch what happens next.

steps.caption: Price pulls back toward the active demand zone.
A 5M candle closes below the zone’s low, its far edge. The setup is invalid.
Later, price drifts back into the old zone. It’s a dead zone now, so this is still not an entry.

check.prompt: Price is back inside the old demand zone. Do you enter?

options.label: Yes. Price returned to the zone, so that’s the retest
options.feedback: A retest only counts while the zone is still valid. A 5M candle already closed below its low, so you don’t keep treating it as an entry.

options.label: No. The zone was invalidated, so it’s no longer an entry
options.why: Right. Once a 5M candle closed below the zone’s low, the setup was invalid. Price coming back doesn’t bring it back to life.

slides.headline: Now the mirror: supply breaks upward.
slides.line: For supply, the far edge is the zone’s high. Press the button and judge the latest candle.

steps.caption: Watch the last candle. Where did it close?

check.prompt: Where did the latest 5M candle close, and what does that mean?

options.label: Above the zone’s high. The setup is invalid
options.why: Yes. A 5M candle closed above the supply zone’s high, its far edge. Don’t keep treating this zone as an entry opportunity.

options.label: Inside the zone. This is the retest
options.feedback: Look again. That candle didn’t stop inside the zone. It closed above the zone’s high, so the setup is invalid.

slides.headline: Price comes back. The zone stays dead.
slides.line: Press the button to mark the close beyond, then play the rest of the chart.

steps.caption: Closed beyond. The zone turns grey. The setup is invalid.
Price falls back toward the old zone. It looks tempting, but the setup is over. No trade.

slides.headline: No BOS #2 means no sequence.
slides.line: Bearish context. Press the button to play the 15M, then the 5M.

steps.caption: BOS #1 (break of structure). A 15M candle closes below the 15M level.
Correction #1. Price pulls back up on the 5M.
Price never closes below the low Correction #1 pulled back from. BOS #2 never happens.

check.prompt: Is there a supply zone to trade here?

options.label: Yes. BOS #1 was bearish, so sell the pullback
options.feedback: Don’t enter simply because BOS #1 occurred. BOS #2 never happened, so there’s no Correction #2, no zone and no BOS #3.

options.label: No. Without BOS #2 there’s no Correction #2 and no zone
options.why: Right. The sequence stopped after Correction #1. Correction #2 creates the zone, and it never had the chance to form.

slides.headline: A potential zone isn’t an active zone.
slides.line: Bullish context. BOS #1, BOS #2 and Correction #2 all happened. Find the zone candle, then read what happens after it.
slides.ask: Tap the last bearish candle of Correction #2: the potential demand zone.
slides.why: That’s the potential demand zone. Now look to the right. Buyers never close above the high Correction #2 pulled back from, so BOS #3 never happens and the zone never activates.

after.caption: The zone stays potential. A zone is not activated just because the opposite-colour candle appeared. No BOS #3, no trade.

slides.headline: Price touched a potential zone. Is that a retest?
slides.line: Correction #2 left a bearish candle. BOS #3 hasn’t happened, and price trades back into that candle’s range.

versus.label: Active zone
points: A return to the zone is a retest.

versus.label: Potential zone
points: A return is not a retest.

check.prompt: Price trades into the potential demand zone before any BOS #3. What do you do?

options.label: Enter, price is in the zone
options.feedback: The zone isn’t active. A zone is not activated merely because the opposite-colour candle appeared. BOS #3 must occur first.

options.label: Nothing yet. Without BOS #3, there is no trade
options.why: Exactly. BOS #3 must occur before the retest-entry model applies.

slides.quote: A dead zone doesn’t come back to life. Let it go.

slides.prompt: In your own words, what makes a setup invalid, and what makes it incomplete?
slides.modelAnswer: A setup is invalid when, after BOS #3, a 5M candle closes beyond the zone’s far edge: below a demand zone’s low or above a supply zone’s high. Even if price comes back later, it’s not an entry. A setup is incomplete when the sequence never finishes, for example when BOS #2 or BOS #3 never happens. Without the full sequence, there is no trade.
